question.problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]?
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{4} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns.
